#+TITLE: Differentiable Polish — gradient-based local refinement after DIRECT, the z-signal, and what is actually transferable to a hand-written CUDA stack
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: differentiable-polish

* Summary

A gradient-polish stage after DIRECT is feasible in this stack, but only if it optimizes a *smooth surrogate* — the production DIRECT_DILATION cost is a piecewise-constant function of pose (binary silhouette + int-atomic reductions), so its gradient is zero almost everywhere and undefined at pixel flips. The surrogate already exists in the codebase: the chamfer distance-map term (DistanceMapMetric), whose gradient is the standard analytic-silhouette-gradient: Σ over rendered edge pixels of ∇D(p)·(projection Jacobian). That Jacobian needs only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that FillTriangleKernel already computes and throws away. The depth channel is the angle's main myth to puncture: a front-surface z/w buffer is 80% machinery-present (the DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z), but a depth channel does *not* make z observable in single-plane fluoro — the 6.31 mm z gap is the magnification limit, and the only real z-fixes are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior. Verdict: GO for a budget-accounted polish stage (chamfer surrogate, analytic Jacobian, ~2-3 weeks) scored by angle 03's harness as a DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish ablation arm; NO-GO for the photometric DRR-gradient and torch-bridge routes.

* Key Findings

** The production cost is piecewise-constant in pose — the gradient of the existing cost is not a usable signal, and this is the load-bearing constraint on everything else
- FastImplantDilationMetric reduces with int atomicAdd over binary comparisons (DILATED_PIXEL/EDGE_PIXEL vs WHITE in the dilated comparison) and DistanceMapMetric sums int distance values over a *discrete* edge-pixel set; both change only when a rendered pixel flips 0↔255 as vertices cross pixel centers. The render itself (RenderEngine::Render) writes a binary silhouette. [Source: repo — src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-92]
- Consequence: finite-difference on the production cost gives zero or garbage Jacobians for any step not straddling a flip boundary; there is no gradient to "polish" through the production metric. Any polish stage must (a) optimize a smooth surrogate, and (b) verify the result with the production cost — the surrogate is a *search* objective, the production cost stays the *arbiter* (same relationship as angle 03's appearance gate vs cost math).
- Also note the existing metric's int reduction truncates (double→int atomicAdd truncation is already listed as bug 6 in the local recon) — a polish surrogate must use float accumulation.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: kills option (b) of accountable question 1 (finite-difference on the existing cost) before it starts; forces the surrogate architecture that the harness can actually measure.

** The smooth surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a chamfer loss, and its gradient is the standard analytic silhouette gradient
- DistanceMapMetric = Σ_{rendered edge pixels} distance_map[p] / (count+0.1) — a mean-chamfer of the rendered silhouette edge to the target (fluoro) edge; the distance transform makes it Lipschitz with an image-space gradient ∇D computable numerically from the distance map itself. [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu; include/compute/frame.h (SetDistanceMap)]
- The standard differentiable-registration gradient is dL/dθ = Σ_{p ∈ E(θ)} ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ) + a boundary term from pixels crossing the edge set; the boundary term is what analytic AA (Modular Primitives) or soft coverage (SoftRas/DIB-R) smooths, and it is small relative to the ∇D term inside the DIRECT basin (few flips per step at convergence). Published relatives of exactly this gradient: "Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation" (arXiv:1906.07870) and "3D/2D Registration of Angiograms using Silhouette-based Differentiable Rendering" (arXiv:2501.14918). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.14918]
- dp/dθ is analytic for a rigid body: projected p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy) with (X,Y,Z) affine in the pose θ (R·v + t), so the 2×6 projection Jacobian is a ~50-line kernel. This is the "Modular-Primitives-style analytic silhouette gradient" in its minimal form — no soft rasterizer, no AA pass required for the MVP.
- Confidence: high (the math is standard; the codebase already contains both ingredients)
- Relevance: this is the minimal viable gradient signal (accountable question 1): analytic projection Jacobian + numerical ∇D from the existing distance map, at 1 render per step. The honest baseline to implement *first* (measurement-first) is forward/central differences on this same surrogate (6-12 renders/step, zero new rasterizer code) — it establishes whether gradient polish wins at all before the analytic investment.

** FillTriangleKernel already computes the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that the gradient needs — and discards them
- FillTriangleKernel computes the unnormalized barycentrics (a, b, c, denominator) for the inside test and only writes 255 to the image. Writing (triangleIndex, a, b, c) out for filled pixels is the Modular-Primitives per-pixel output minus the NDC z: exactly the (ID, u, v) tuple the backward pass consumes. The renderer also knows the projected positions and (in the DRR twin) per-vertex camera z, so the un-projected 3D source point of each edge pixel is recoverable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel; Modular Primitives rasterizer outputs (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + 2×2 barycentric Jacobian per https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
- Cost: one extra device buffer (float4 per filled pixel) + ~10 lines in the fill kernel. The stride/prefix/bounding-box launch scheme is untouched.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance: this is what makes the analytic route cheap — the rasterizer is already 80% of a differentiable rasterizer; only the output staging and the backward scatter-add are missing.

** The depth channel: machinery is 80% present, but a depth channel does NOT fix the z-weak axis in single-plane fluoro — the honest finding this angle exists to deliver
- Where z comes from today: the silhouette path (Render) computes per-vertex camera z (tZ) in WorldToPixelKernel and *discards it*; the DRR path stores it (dev_transf_vertex_zs_) and DRR_FillTriangleKernel interpolates per-pixel perspective-correct z via the rational formula (tvz1·tvz2·tvz3·denominator)/(a·tvz2·tvz3 + b·tvz1·tvz3 + c·tvz1·tvz2) — which is exactly 1/(λ1/z1 + λ2/z2 + λ3/z3), i.e. the perspective-correct interpolated camera z at the pixel. There is no z-testing anywhere (all triangles draw; backfaces are sign-flipped in the DRR accumulation). A front-surface NDC-style depth buffer (this stack's "z/w" ≡ −tZ_cam, positive toward the detector) needs only a min-z test in the fill + a float buffer — and dev_z_line_values_ (width×height float) is already allocated and reusable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu:430-520, src/compute/render_drr_engine.cu DRR_WorldToPixelKernel + DRR_FillTriangleKernel, include/compute/render_engine.cuh dev_z_line_values_/dev_transf_vertex_zs_]
- Why it does not fix z: (a) there is *no target depth* in a single-plane fluoro to compare a rendered depth against — a depth-difference term only exists in synthetic self-supervised ablations (render at known pose → optimize), against a registered bone model / known-geometry prior, or in biplane; (b) the observed z gap is the magnification limit — z-translation is only observable through scale (6.31 mm z gap vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane in baseline.json; angle 03's probe arithmetic: <1% scale change over ±15 mm at ~1.1 m), and no gradient changes what is observable; (c) NVDiffrast — the reference implementation of Modular Primitives — intentionally does *not* backprop through the z/w channel (issue #70: the z/w output's gradients are not propagated; the meaningful gradients are the vertex-position ones). [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances.observed_max_gap_vs_golden; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70 (search-verified content, page fetch failed); https://nvlabs.github.io/nvdiffrast/]
- What the depth machinery IS worth: (i) occlusion-aware visibility gradients — Modular Primitives' premise "a 3D primitive with no effect on the image receives zero gradient" requires knowing which triangle owns each pixel (z-test), which the renderer lacks today; (ii) a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm (a genuine z test *when a target depth exists*); (iii) the z-line-integral (dev_z_line_values_) is a stronger quantitative z signal than front-depth (it shifts by ≈Δz·path-length under z-translation) but is an X-ray-attenuation proxy — unobservable for a saturated metal implant and only useful in the ML/DRR pathway (DiffDRR-style).
- The real z-fixes: biplane (the codebase already has it — calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B and a biplane branch in DIRECT_DILATION) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone). This matches the prior-run ML angle's finding 8 ("if the ML pathway is to beat the monoplane z gap, biplane is the evidence-backed direction").
- Confidence: high on the machinery facts (source-verified + NVDiffrast issue); high on the observability argument (analytic); medium on the exact clinical z-benefit of biplane/prior until measured
- Relevance: answer to accountable question 2 — the depth channel is a *gradient-quality and ablation-signal* feature, not a z fix; the harness should test it as such (self-supervised depth arm), and the z-profile probe (angle 03) should first confirm the chamfer surrogate's valley is deeper than the dilated-overlap valley — that is the precondition for any polish z-win.

** Feasibility verdicts per idea (accountable question 1 + 2, with effort/risk — accountable question 3)

MVP = forward-difference gradient on the surrogate (6 renders/step, ~1 week) then analytic projection Jacobian + ∇D kernel (1 render/step, +1 week), reusing Render(), the uploaded distance maps, and the injected-cost lambda. Risk medium-low: all machinery exists; the known index-formula bug in distance_map_metric.cu:27 (blockIdx.y+gridDim.x instead of blockIdx.y*gridDim.x) must NOT be copied into new kernels; float accumulation replaces int; match the production backface config (true) and leaf dilation (1) for consistency with verification.

- Analytic AA / occlusion-aware coverage gradient (Modular-Primitives-style, 4×4-style tiles) — research increment (+2-4 weeks) after the MVP shows a win; requires the z-test ownership first. Do not start before measurement.

- Torch bridge (thin autograd extension) — NO-GO on convention and merit: torch is *already linked into jtml_compute* (machine_learning_tools.cpp is in the lib, and CostFunctionManager.h even includes <ATen/ops/div_native.h>), so the dependency is not the objection — but for 6-DoF pose of a static STL, autograd buys nothing (the rasterizer backward is a scatter-add; Modular Primitives' core is a CUDA primitive library, torch is only the wrapper) and it violates the documented "no torch in the cost path" design. The ATen include in CostFunctionManager.h is a smell to flag to 04-backend-architecture. [Source: repo — src/compute/CMakeLists.txt:45, include/compute/CostFunctionManager.h, src/compute/machine_learning_tools.cpp]

- Loop shape: DIRECT trunk (20k) → 2× branch (5k each) → leaf (5k) → RunPolishStage(current_optimum_location_) → optional re-seed: if polish improves the production cost, run one more leaf-range DIRECT around the polished pose (the DIRECT+local-search re-seed pattern from the literature: Gablonsky's locally-biased DIRECT, the DIRECT+DF-local-search hybrids). #+TITLE: Differentiable Polish — gradient-based local refinement after DIRECT, the z-signal, and what is actually transferable to a hand-written CUDA stack
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: differentiable-polish

* Summary

A gradient-polish stage after DIRECT is feasible in this stack, but only if it optimizes a *smooth surrogate* — the production DIRECT_DILATION cost is a piecewise-constant function of pose (binary silhouette + int-atomic reductions), so its gradient is zero almost everywhere and undefined at pixel flips. The surrogate already exists in the codebase: the chamfer distance-map term (DistanceMapMetric), whose gradient is the standard analytic-silhouette-gradient: Σ over rendered edge pixels of ∇D(p)·(projection Jacobian). That Jacobian needs only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that FillTriangleKernel already computes and throws away. The depth channel is the angle's main myth to puncture: a front-surface z/w buffer is 80% machinery-present (the DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z), but a depth channel does *not* make z observable in single-plane fluoro — the 6.31 mm z gap is the magnification limit, and the only real z-fixes are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior. Verdict: GO for a budget-accounted polish stage (chamfer surrogate, analytic Jacobian, ~2-3 weeks) scored by angle 03's harness as a DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish ablation arm; NO-GO for the photometric DRR-gradient and torch-bridge routes.

* Key Findings

** The production cost is piecewise-constant in pose — the gradient of the existing cost is not a usable signal, and this is the load-bearing constraint on everything else
- FastImplantDilationMetric reduces with int atomicAdd over binary comparisons (DILATED_PIXEL/EDGE_PIXEL vs WHITE in the dilated comparison) and DistanceMapMetric sums int distance values over a *discrete* edge-pixel set; both change only when a rendered pixel flips 0↔255 as vertices cross pixel centers. The render itself (RenderEngine::Render) writes a binary silhouette. [Source: repo — src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-92]
- Consequence: finite-difference on the production cost gives zero or garbage Jacobians for any step not straddling a flip boundary; there is no gradient to "polish" through the production metric. Any polish stage must (a) optimize a smooth surrogate, and (b) verify the result with the production cost — the surrogate is a *search* objective, the production cost stays the *arbiter* (same relationship as angle 03's appearance gate vs cost math).
- Also note the existing metric's int reduction truncates (double→int atomicAdd truncation is already listed as bug 6 in the local recon) — a polish surrogate must use float accumulation.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: kills option (b) of accountable question 1 (finite-difference on the existing cost) before it starts; forces the surrogate architecture that the harness can actually measure.

** The smooth surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a chamfer loss, and its gradient is the standard analytic silhouette gradient
- DistanceMapMetric = Σ_{rendered edge pixels} distance_map[p] / (count+0.1) — a mean-chamfer of the rendered silhouette edge to the target (fluoro) edge; the distance transform makes it Lipschitz with an image-space gradient ∇D computable numerically from the distance map itself. [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu; include/compute/frame.h (SetDistanceMap)]
- The standard differentiable-registration gradient is dL/dθ = Σ_{p ∈ E(θ)} ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ) + a boundary term from pixels crossing the edge set; the boundary term is what analytic AA (Modular Primitives) or soft coverage (SoftRas/DIB-R) smooths, and it is small relative to the ∇D term inside the DIRECT basin (few flips per step at convergence). Published relatives of exactly this gradient: "Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation" (arXiv:1906.07870) and "3D/2D Registration of Angiograms using Silhouette-based Differentiable Rendering" (arXiv:2501.14918). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.14918]
- dp/dθ is analytic for a rigid body: projected p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy) with (X,Y,Z) affine in the pose θ (R·v + t), so the 2×6 projection Jacobian is a ~50-line kernel. This is the "Modular-Primitives-style analytic silhouette gradient" in its minimal form — no soft rasterizer, no AA pass required for the MVP.
- Confidence: high (the math is standard; the codebase already contains both ingredients)
- Relevance: this is the minimal viable gradient signal (accountable question 1): analytic projection Jacobian + numerical ∇D from the existing distance map, at 1 render per step. The honest baseline to implement *first* (measurement-first) is forward/central differences on this same surrogate (6-12 renders/step, zero new rasterizer code) — it establishes whether gradient polish wins at all before the analytic investment.

** FillTriangleKernel already computes the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that the gradient needs — and discards them
- FillTriangleKernel computes the unnormalized barycentrics (a, b, c, denominator) for the inside test and only writes 255 to the image. Writing (triangleIndex, a, b, c) out for filled pixels is the Modular-Primitives per-pixel output minus the NDC z: exactly the (ID, u, v) tuple the backward pass consumes. The renderer also knows the projected positions and (in the DRR twin) per-vertex camera z, so the un-projected 3D source point of each edge pixel is recoverable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel; Modular Primitives rasterizer outputs (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + 2×2 barycentric Jacobian per https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
- Cost: one extra device buffer (float4 per filled pixel) + ~10 lines in the fill kernel. The stride/prefix/bounding-box launch scheme is untouched.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance: this is what makes the analytic route cheap — the rasterizer is already 80% of a differentiable rasterizer; only the output staging and the backward scatter-add are missing.

** The depth channel: machinery is 80% present, but a depth channel does NOT fix the z-weak axis in single-plane fluoro — the honest finding this angle exists to deliver
- Where z comes from today: the silhouette path (Render) computes per-vertex camera z (tZ) in WorldToPixelKernel and *discards it*; the DRR path stores it (dev_transf_vertex_zs_) and DRR_FillTriangleKernel interpolates per-pixel perspective-correct z via the rational formula (tvz1·tvz2·tvz3·denominator)/(a·tvz2·tvz3 + b·tvz1·tvz3 + c·tvz1·tvz2) — which is exactly 1/(λ1/z1 + λ2/z2 + λ3/z3), i.e. the perspective-correct interpolated camera z at the pixel. There is no z-testing anywhere (all triangles draw; backfaces are sign-flipped in the DRR accumulation). A front-surface NDC-style depth buffer (this stack's "z/w" ≡ −tZ_cam, positive toward the detector) needs only a min-z test in the fill + a float buffer — and dev_z_line_values_ (width×height float) is already allocated and reusable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu:430-520, src/compute/render_drr_engine.cu DRR_WorldToPixelKernel + DRR_FillTriangleKernel, include/compute/render_engine.cuh dev_z_line_values_/dev_transf_vertex_zs_]
- Why it does not fix z: (a) there is *no target depth* in a single-plane fluoro to compare a rendered depth against — a depth-difference term only exists in synthetic self-supervised ablations (render at known pose → optimize), against a registered bone model / known-geometry prior, or in biplane; (b) the observed z gap is the magnification limit — z-translation is only observable through scale (6.31 mm z gap vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane in baseline.json; angle 03's probe arithmetic: <1% scale change over ±15 mm at ~1.1 m), and no gradient changes what is observable; (c) NVDiffrast — the reference implementation of Modular Primitives — intentionally does *not* backprop through the z/w channel (issue #70: the z/w output's gradients are not propagated; the meaningful gradients are the vertex-position ones). [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances.observed_max_gap_vs_golden; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70 (search-verified content, page fetch failed); https://nvlabs.github.io/nvdiffrast/]
- What the depth machinery IS worth: (i) occlusion-aware visibility gradients — Modular Primitives' premise "a 3D primitive with no effect on the image receives zero gradient" requires knowing which triangle owns each pixel (z-test), which the renderer lacks today; (ii) a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm (a genuine z test *when a target depth exists*); (iii) the z-line-integral (dev_z_line_values_) is a stronger quantitative z signal than front-depth (it shifts by ≈Δz·path-length under z-translation) but is an X-ray-attenuation proxy — unobservable for a saturated metal implant and only useful in the ML/DRR pathway (DiffDRR-style).
- The real z-fixes: biplane (the codebase already has it — calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B and a biplane branch in DIRECT_DILATION) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone). This matches the prior-run ML angle's finding 8 ("if the ML pathway is to beat the monoplane z gap, biplane is the evidence-backed direction").
- Confidence: high on the machinery facts (source-verified + NVDiffrast issue); high on the observability argument (analytic); medium on the exact clinical z-benefit of biplane/prior until measured
- Relevance: answer to accountable question 2 — the depth channel is a *gradient-quality and ablation-signal* feature, not a z fix; the harness should test it as such (self-supervised depth arm), and the z-profile probe (angle 03) should first confirm the chamfer surrogate's valley is deeper than the dilated-overlap valley — that is the precondition for any polish z-win.

** Feasibility verdicts per idea (accountable question 1 + 2, with effort/risk — accountable question 3)
- Silhouette-gradient polish on the chamfer surrogate — GO. MVP = forward-difference gradient on the surrogate (6 renders/step, ~1 week) then analytic projection Jacobian + ∇D kernel (1 render/step, +1 week), reusing Render(), the uploaded distance maps, and the injected-cost lambda. Risk medium-low: all machinery exists; the known index-formula bug in distance_map_metric.cu:27 (blockIdx.y+gridDim.x instead of blockIdx.y*gridDim.x) must NOT be copied into new kernels; float accumulation replaces int; match the production backface config (true) and leaf dilation (1) for consistency with verification.
- NDC z/w depth buffer — feasible machinery (+1 week: min-z test + float buffer reuse), but NOT a z fix; only pursue as the enabler for occlusion-aware gradients (visibility gradients) or the synthetic-depth ablation arm. Risk low.

The ATen include in CostFunctionManager.h is a smell to flag to 04-backend-architecture. #+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+ROUND: 2 (wave 1) — angles 01–04 deepened with '## Round 2' sections; 05/06 deferred to wave 2
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

The recommended course of action, in dependency order, is unchanged in shape and updated in content: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, behavior-neutral fixes, the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline — plus the new CUDA-free finite-check at DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction, needed regardless of GLh); (2) the measurement apparatus per angle 03 — the z-profile probe on the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (now an executable 31-render spec) and the production-shaped multi-stage oracle through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam, which **no longer needs the "small seam addition"**: Round 2 proved Directive::SymTrap already exists in the typed enum, so the tibia-ambiguity pass is three pins, not a code change; (3) the ablation runner + ablation.json (schema now complete, plus the perturbation suite that calibrates the IoU gate's checked coverage); (4) the evidence-backed algorithm upgrade from angle 01 — **1-DTC-GL-gb** — now with a concrete analytic battery (22 n=5 problems + Hartman6, GKLS classes, pe≤1e-2), a quantified split tie-break divergence (a faithful GL landing requires switching the repo's largest-denormalized-side rule to the study's least-split rule), and a gb-semantics caveat (the DIRECTGO reference code toggles the phases inverted relative to the paper's prose — implement the canonical semantics plus an ablation arm replicating the code as shipped); (5) compute-perf cuts 0–4 per angle 05, gated on oracle green and bit-identical cost values; (6) the differentiable-polish stage per angle 06, GO-gated on the z-profile probe and an ablation arm. Architecture work (angle 04) flows through as additive cuts A–F.

Two tensions the user should carry explicitly. First, **the variant switch cannot fix the z-axis**: Round 2 resolved this from a scoping tension into an explicit mechanism analysis — the variant choice (search scheme) and the z-sensitivity ranking (cost observability) are orthogonal in mechanism, with only two documented second-order interactions (the NaN/Inf trigger and refinement-control savings on z-flat costs); the harness must report evals and z-error separately, and a variant-switch win must never be read as a z fix. The real z remedies remain biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior, and every z remedy is gated on angle 03's probe. Second, **perf cuts do not sacrifice determinism**: every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd (order-independent, value-deterministic), so async copies and iteration batching can preserve bit-identical results; angle 04's Round-2 seam contract pins the double-buffered eval state (compute owns the buffer state, the manager owns the object graph, the domain sees only std::function).

Round 2 also closed the run's longest-standing open question: **the DIRECT-GLh NaN trigger is now resolved per-variant.** DIRECT_DILATION is structurally incapable of emitting NaN/Inf (all-int composition, +0.1-guarded division, max accumulation 2.55e8 ≪ 2³¹) — the GLh trigger lives in DIRECT_MAHFOUZ (0/0 via the pointer-guard bug, production-reachable), DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT (UB min_dist), and sym_trap (asin domain). The finite-check belongs at the one shared chokepoint, DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction (direct_optimizer.cpp:205), and the round-1 claim that "NaN poisons hull slope comparisons" is corrected: NaN boxes accumulate as dead weight at the column front (lost evals, unbounded growth), with the column minimum poisoned only after all finite boxes are trisected away — a delayed, conditional effect, still worth closing. The "12x fewer evals" polish thesis remains a target to test, not a justification: angle 06's analysis puts the realistic win at ~1.5–3× in the leaf/refinement phase, with the chamfer distance-map surrogate as the one smooth gradient signal. Everything else from the papers — 1-DTDV boundary sampling, analytic-AA occlusion gradients, DRR-photometric gradients, torch bridges — stays conditional, deferred, or NO-GO, and each lands only through the harness.

* Round 2 Updates (wave 1)

This section records the Round-2 deltas (what changed since the round-1 synthesis). The folded-in detail lives in Key Findings, Contradictions, and Recommendations below; this section is the diff.

** Deltas by angle

*** Angle 01 — DIRECT variant surface (Round 2)
- gb phase-switch: numbers are canonical (5 non-improving iterations / security every 5th, from Gb-DISIMPL, ref [28]) — resolving round 1's "recommended values [10,28]" (those are bibliography references [10]=Gb-BIRECT 2020, [28]=Gb-DISIMPL 2014, not parameter values). NEW docs-vs-code contradiction: DIRECTGO's I_DTC_GL.m 'gb' branch toggles the phases inverted relative to the paper prose and all sibling ports; the paper's 0.7840 success figure may have been produced by either semantics (unverifiable). Implement the canonical semantics + a code-as-shipped ablation arm + a gb-semantics pin (a two-phase/global-only iteration trace on a stalled quadratic). [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-1]
- Split tie-break: the study's least-split-so-far (unit space) rule diverges from the repo's largest-denormalized-side rule on the FIRST branch/leaf split (Z vs X, deterministically); landing 1-DTC-GL-gb faithfully REQUIRES the least-split rule + global split counter — a real behavior change, with the battery probes specified (Tier-0 least-split pin, anisotropic-range probe with the actual stage ranges, perturbed-domain DIRECTGOLib problems). [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-2]
- Analytic battery concretized: 22 n=5 problems + Hartman6 (n=6) with f* formulas, the 15/22 f*=0 subset reported separately, GKLS 8 classes with standard d/r/h parameters, pe≤1e-2 termination, crossover budgets 500/1000/4000 paper-anchored (100 is a JTML harness choice, flagged), DIRECTGOLib version pin (v1.2 primary, v1.1 for cross-checking the study's numbers). [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-3]
- GLh: exact surrogate φ = f_min + d_unit(x_min,x) with d̄ = d/√n; DenormalizeFromCenter must NOT feed the surrogate distance (a mixed-unit slip exists even in the reference sDirect_GLh.m — do not replicate); the NaN-path analysis is corrected (dead-weight accumulation, not immediate hull-slope poisoning); the finite-check + feasibility flag is needed regardless of GLh. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-4]
- 1-DTDV boundary probe: explicit construction (Deb02 on [0,1]^n, shifted-Levy ν) and a two-part go/no-go (analytic ν≥4/6 win with bounded interior regression AND production z-profile edge detection); default NO-GO. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-5]
- Contradiction 2 resolved at the mechanism level: variant choice and z-sensitivity are orthogonal; two second-order interactions documented; the battery reports evals and z-error separately. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-6]

*** Angle 02 — Cost-path foundation (Round 2)
- NaN/Inf audit: DIRECT_DILATION structurally cannot emit NaN/Inf (all-int composition, +0.1-guarded division, max 2.55e8 ≪ 2³¹); the emitters are DIRECT_MAHFOUZ (0/0 pointer-guard, production-reachable, forces dilation 3), DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT (UB min_dist), sym_trap (asin domain). Finite-check design at DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction (direct_optimizer.cpp:205) — the one shared chokepoint (production/oracle/coordinator), CUDA-free; non_finite_count_ + GLh surrogate hook + GetNonFiniteCount; headless (Tier-0) and adversarial GPU (Tier-2) probes specified; six failure modes code-grounded (int overflow ruled out). [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
- Distance-map index fix impact: exactly one reader; post-optimize metrics NOT corrupted; corruption shape = top-band exclusion + middle-band multiplicity weighting → systematically flatter in z; expected re-baseline direction = recovered z moves toward fem.jts, |z gap| shrinks (6.31 mm frame-1 gap expected to shrink materially); magnitude not predictable. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
- Backface mechanism correction: culling ON paints 1-px speckle per backface triangle (size 1, not 0) and the image bbox is ON/OFF-identical → the ON-vs-OFF IoU is a clean same-crop comparison; KR_right_7_fem.stl verified ASCII MATLAB stlwrite, exactly 12,412 facets; the watertightness check + ON-vs-OFF IoU protocol are now executable specs (0.99 threshold); NEW finding IOU(∅,∅) = 0/0 NaN (iou.cu:82-83) — Tier-0 reference decision point (recommend 1.0 as spec-with-flagged-deviation). [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
- Mahfouz normalization decoded: 2.55 = 255/100 exact (0–100 dilated-edge scale → 0–255); the final contour ratio is 255·Σ(trunc(2.55·p)·c)/Σ(trunc(2.55·p)) — the 2.55 cancels, leaving a small per-pixel truncation bias; the −2.67 contour-vs-intensity weight has NO in-repo rationale — the piece the 2003 paper (Zotero target identified: TMI 22(12):1561–1574, DOI 10.1109/TMI.2003.820027, PMID 14649746) must arbitrate; kernel-as-spec decision rule (3 conditions for the paper to override). [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]

#+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+ROUND: 2 (wave 1) — angles 01–04 deepened with '## Round 2' sections; 05/06 deferred to wave 2
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

The recommended course of action, in dependency order, is unchanged in shape and updated in content: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, behavior-neutral fixes, the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline — plus the new CUDA-free finite-check at DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction, needed regardless of GLh); (2) the measurement apparatus per angle 03 — the z-profile probe on the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (now an executable 31-render spec) and the production-shaped multi-stage oracle through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam, which **no longer needs the "small seam addition"**: Round 2 proved Directive::SymTrap already exists in the typed enum, so the tibia-ambiguity pass is three pins, not a code change; (3) the ablation runner + ablation.json (schema now complete, plus the perturbation suite that calibrates the IoU gate's checked coverage); (4) the evidence-backed algorithm upgrade from angle 01 — **1-DTC-GL-gb** — now with a concrete analytic battery (22 n=5 problems + Hartman6, GKLS classes, pe≤1e-2), a quantified split tie-break divergence (a faithful GL landing requires switching the repo's largest-denormalized-side rule to the study's least-split rule), and a gb-semantics caveat (the DIRECTGO reference code toggles the phases inverted relative to the paper's prose — implement the canonical semantics plus an ablation arm replicating the code as shipped); (5) compute-perf cuts 0–4 per angle 05, gated on oracle green and bit-identical cost values; (6) the differentiable-polish stage per angle 06, GO-gated on the z-profile probe and an ablation arm. Architecture work (angle 04) flows through as additive cuts A–F.

Two tensions the user should carry explicitly. First, **the variant switch cannot fix the z-axis**: Round 2 resolved this from a scoping tension into an explicit mechanism analysis — the variant choice (search scheme) and the z-sensitivity ranking (cost observability) are orthogonal in mechanism, with only two documented second-order interactions (the NaN/Inf trigger and refinement-control savings on z-flat costs); the harness must report evals and z-error separately, and a variant-switch win must never be read as a z fix. The real z remedies remain biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior, and every z remedy is gated on angle 03's probe. Second, **perf cuts do not sacrifice determinism**: every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd (order-independent, value-deterministic), so async copies and iteration batching can preserve bit-identical results; angle 04's Round-2 seam contract pins the double-buffered eval state (compute owns the buffer state, the manager owns the object graph, the domain sees only std::function).

Round 2 also closed the run's longest-standing open question: **the DIRECT-GLh NaN trigger is now resolved per-variant.** DIRECT_DILATION is structurally incapable of emitting NaN/Inf (all-int composition, +0.1-guarded division, max accumulation 2.55e8 ≪ 2³¹) — the GLh trigger lives in DIRECT_MAHFOUZ (0/0 via the pointer-guard bug, production-reachable), DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT (UB min_dist), and sym_trap (asin domain). The finite-check belongs at the one shared chokepoint, DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction (direct_optimizer.cpp:205), and the round-1 claim that "NaN poisons hull slope comparisons" is corrected: NaN boxes accumulate as dead weight at the column front (lost evals, unbounded growth), with the column minimum poisoned only after all finite boxes are trisected away — a delayed, conditional effect, still worth closing. The "12x fewer evals" polish thesis remains a target to test, not a justification: angle 06's analysis puts the realistic win at ~1.5–3× in the leaf/refinement phase, with the chamfer distance-map surrogate as the one smooth gradient signal. Everything else from the papers — 1-DTDV boundary sampling, analytic-AA occlusion gradients, DRR-photometric gradients, torch bridges — stays conditional, deferred, or NO-GO, and each lands only through the harness.

* Round 2 Updates (wave 1)

This section records the Round-2 deltas (what changed since the round-1 synthesis). The folded-in detail lives in Key Findings, Contradictions, and Recommendations below; this section is the diff.

** Deltas by angle

*** Angle 01 — DIRECT variant surface (Round 2)
- gb phase-switch: numbers are canonical (5 non-improving iterations / security every 5th, from Gb-DISIMPL, ref [28]) — resolving round 1's "recommended values [10,28]" (those are bibliography references [10]=Gb-BIRECT 2020, [28]=Gb-DISIMPL 2014, not parameter values). NEW docs-vs-code contradiction: DIRECTGO's I_DTC_GL.m 'gb' branch toggles the phases inverted relative to the paper prose and all sibling ports; the paper's 0.7840 success figure may have been produced by either semantics (unverifiable). Implement the canonical semantics + a code-as-shipped ablation arm + a gb-semantics pin (a two-phase/global-only iteration trace on a stalled quadratic). [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-1]

Verdict: DIRECT_DILATION returns a finite double for EVERY pose, including empty silhouettes, degenerate projections, and behind-camera poses. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2 "NaN/Inf emission audit"]
- The emitters, all production-reachable: (1) DIRECT_MAHFOUZ — `if (pixel_score_ != 0)` tests the pinned pointer, never the value (implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324/446); with pixel_score_[0] == 0 the divisions give 0/0 NaN (selectable in production, forces dilation 3, optimizer_manager.cpp:252-253/270-271/288-289); (2) DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT — UB min_dist read can surface a NaN payload (compiler-dependent); (3) sym_trap — asin(fem2tib[2][1]) is NaN for |entry| > 1 (sym_trap_function.cpp:129), reachable through FP rounding. Int overflow and the DRR float-atomic path are ruled out. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
- Correction to the round-1/synthesis claim "NaN poisons hull slope comparisons": the data storage sorts each size-column descending (true minimum at the back); ConvexHull reads only the back. A NaN box fails every comparison and is inserted at the column FRONT — never selected, never popped (pops the back), never read by the hull. Actual NaN behavior: (a) `result < current_optimum_value_` is false, so a NaN eval never updates the optimum; (b) the NaN box accumulates as dead weight (lost evals, unbounded growth); (c) the column minimum becomes NaN only after all finite boxes in that column are trisected away — delayed, conditional poisoning. The finite-check is motivated by (a)+(b), not the round-1 claim. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2; src/domain/direct_data_storage.cpp:92-131]
- The finite-check wraps DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction (direct_optimizer.cpp:205) — the single chokepoint shared by production (RunDirectStage), the oracle, and the coordinator; CUDA-free (headless-testable), one std::isfinite per eval. Design: `if (!std::isfinite(result)) { non_finite_count_++; /* GLh: result = f_min + d(x,x_min) when enabled; else treat as infeasible (do not store, never wins the optimum) */ }` plus GetNonFiniteCount() and an iteration-callback event. The GPU side needs NO checks — all GPU outputs are provably finite ints. Probes: Tier-0 headless (fake cost lambda returning NaN/±Inf/sNaN; asserts no crash, counter increments, optimum never reflects a non-finite eval, GLh surrogate behavior, surviving columns finite) and Tier-2 GPU (sanity sweep golden ± range ~61 evals; adversarial poses ±200 mm off-axis, behind camera, 90°/180° rotations; assert finite AND cudaGetLastError() == cudaSuccess after each eval — the sticky-error trap at render_engine.cu:713; DIRECT_MAHFOUZ at an empty-silhouette pose EXPECT NaN today, green after the guard fix). Six failure modes code-grounded (degenerate projection, zero denominator, empty silhouette, uninitialized memory, fragment overflow = mute evals, int overflow ruled out). [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
- Cross-angle consequence: GLh's trigger question (angle 01 Finding 3) is answered — the trigger exists but only outside the oracle's cost, so GLh is conditional on the three emitters, and the finite-check is justified on its own (a latent bug class), independent of GLh. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-4; angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]

Now the analytic projection Jacobian math:
- Pose θ = (tx, ty, tz, rx, ry, rz) (the code uses Z-X-Y Euler: model_rotation_mat_ = Rz·Rx·Ry per SetPose — R = Rz(θz)·Rx(θx)·Ry(θy)).
- For a model-space point v, X = R·v + t, Z = X_z.
- Projection: p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy). Note in the code fx and fy are NEGATIVE for UF calibration (fx_ = −d/pixel_pitch) — that's the image flip convention (screen y up). This matters for the Jacobian signs! dp/dθ = (fx/Z)·dX/dθ − (fx·X/Z²)·dZ/dθ for the x-component (with the fx sign baked in).
- dX/dθ: translation columns are unit vectors: dX/dtx = (1,0,0) etc. Rotation columns: dX/dr_i = dR/dr_i·v, where dR/dr_i for the Z-X-Y composition is computable analytically (6-12 lines of trig). The standard form: ∂p/∂θ is a 2×6 matrix: for each DoF, ∂p_x/∂θ_j = fx·(∂X_j·Z − X·∂Z_j)/Z², ∂p_y/∂θ_j = fy·(∂Y_j·Z − Y·∂Z_j)/Z².
- dL/dθ = Σ_{p ∈ edge(θ)} ∇D(p)·dp/dθ, where ∇D(p) = (D(p+ex) − D(p−ex), D(p+ey) − D(p−ey))/2 numerically from the uint8 distance map (L1 → gradient magnitude ≤ 1; at medial-axis pixels the central difference is 0 — fine).
- Missing boundary term: pixels entering/leaving the edge set under θ-perturbation contribute ∇D(p)·dp/dθ evaluated at the crossing; the standard argument is that inside the DIRECT basin this is second-order small (Modular Primitives' AA and SoftRas' coverage smoothing exist to handle exactly this term; the MVP ignores it and the forward-difference arm is the empirical check that the analytic gradient matches the finite difference on the surrogate to within the quantization floor).

Which z_trans range: the probe's ±15 mm sweep — matching the leaf z-range (±15 mm per settings_constants) and the observed 6.31 mm gap being well inside it. The gate's valley_depth is computed over the full ±15 mm sweep (31 points); additionally the near-field (|Δz| ≤ 6.31 mm) depth is reported so the gate can distinguish "valley at the golden z" from "global slope".

Hmm wait, one more check on the leaf ranges — from angle 01 R2-2: "leaf (3,3,15,3,3,3) — denormalized (6,6,30,6,6,6)". So leaf range in z is ±15 mm, in x/y/r ±3. And probe sweeps ±15 mm at 1 mm steps = 31 renders. OK consistent.

Now the "6-renders-per-step" detail: dispatch says 6 renders/step. As computed: forward differences = f(θ+h e_i) for i=1..6, with f(θ) cached from the previous step's base render. First step costs 7. With a fixed step size and no line search, subsequent steps cost 6. If we add backtracking line search, each rejected trial adds 1 render. The MVP should start WITHOUT line search: fixed step with step-size decay (or a simple 3-point trial: α, α/2, α/4 — but that's still line search). Keep MVP minimal: fixed step α, with a step-halving rule on non-improvement (accept only if the production cost at θ_{k+1} ≤ production cost at θ_k; else halve α and retry, up to 5 halvings, then stop the polish). Each halving trial = 1 surrogate render + 1 verification render. Budget counts both.

Which DOF perturbations: the 6 unit directions e_i in the ORDER (x_loc, y_loc, z_loc, x_ang, y_ang, z_ang) matching Pose's field order. Step sizes as above with per-axis h calibration.

Also the dispatch says "how the existing RenderEngine renders 6 poses": the polish loop calls SetPose(θ + h·e_i) then Render() sequentially on the same RenderEngine instance (or the GPUModel's RenderPrimaryCamera wrapper which calls Render under the hood — in DIRECT_DILATION it's gpu_principal_model_->RenderPrimaryCamera(pose)). Reuse GPUModel::RenderPrimaryCamera — that's the existing seam that the CostFunctionManager uses. So the surrogate eval = RenderPrimaryCamera(pose) + (edge pass + chamfer) — the polish stage calls the SAME GPUModel methods the cost function calls; the 6 renders are just 6 sequential RenderPrimaryCamera calls with perturbed poses. No new render path, no streams (parallel renders across 6 poses would need 6 GPUModels or double-buffered state — that's 05's batching territory; the MVP is sequential).

Wait — one more subtlety about RenderPrimaryCamera: does the GPUModel have a single RenderEngine per camera? RenderPrimaryCamera(pose) presumably calls render_engine_->SetPose(pose); Render(). The polish stage holds the leaf CostFunctionManager (which owns gpu_principal_model_ and gpu_distance_maps_) — so the polish reuses the leaf CFM's GPU objects. Good — that's the round-1 seam (no OptimizerRunLaunch signature change).

Now the concrete numbers for budget: B_p default = 1000 surrogate evals (≈ 100-160 gradient steps at 6-10 evals/step + verification). polish_max_steps = 200 (gradient steps), polish_budget_ = 1000 (eval-call accounting). Settings: enable_polish_/polish_budget_/polish_max_steps mirror enable_leaf_ (round-1 already spec'd). Trust region: the polish starts at the leaf optimum; the leaf range (x,y ±3, z ±15, r ±3) bounds the acceptable region — the polish should CLAMP steps to the leaf box (project the step back into the box), because outside the box the DIRECT search already explored. That's a nice concrete rule: polish explores the leaf box only (the "local refinement" semantics).

Now the verification cadence: verify with the production cost every step (it's cheap relative to... no, verification = full production eval ≈ same cost as a surrogate eval — the production cost eval IS the full pipeline (white_sum is a constant per frame, so production eval = surrogate eval + dilated-overlap difference kernel... hmm, production = white_sum(constant) + FastImplantDilationMetric + DistanceMapMetric; surrogate = FastImplantDilationMetric? No! Wait. I need to re-decide what the surrogate is.

Let me be careful: 
- Production cost (per eval) = white_sum_A (constant per frame) + FastImplantDilationMetric (dilated overlap, piecewise-constant) + DistanceMapMetric (chamfer, smooth-ish).
- The GRADIENT should be of the smooth part: the chamfer term. The dilated-overlap term is piecewise-constant (binary flips) — including it in the gradient target reintroduces the zero-gradient problem. So gradient target f_grad(θ) = DistanceMapMetric(θ) ONLY.
- The ACCEPTANCE criterion for a polish step: production cost (full) at θ_{k+1} ≤ production cost at θ_k (the production cost stays the arbiter — round-1 rule). 
- So per gradient step: 6 surrogate renders (chamfer-only) for the finite-difference gradient (or 1 render for the analytic arm) + 1 verification render (full production cost, which needs white_sum + FastImplant + chamfer — but white_sum is a constant; FastImplantDilationMetric runs its own edge+dilate+difference; the verification render's chamfer isn't needed separately... the full production eval = FastImplant + chamfer on the same render). So the verification eval and a surrogate eval SHARE the render! A verification eval gives you the chamfer value for free. So the step cost: 6 perturbed renders (chamfer-only gradient) + 1 base render (verification + cached base chamfer). Total 7 renders/step (first step), 6 after the first (the base render at θ_k was the previous step's verification). This matches the "6-renders-per-step" in the dispatch. 

For the ANALYTIC arm: 1 render/step (the verification render at θ_k serves as the base for the gradient kernel — the gradient kernel runs on the verification render's image AFTER the edge pass; but careful: the gradient kernel needs the EDGE-marked image and the attribute buffer; the verification render runs the full FastImplantDilationMetric which edge-marks AND dilates in place; the attribute buffer is per-pixel so unaffected by dilation; the gradient kernel reads EDGE pixels — the same pixel set the chamfer value reads. But wait — the verification runs FastImplant FIRST which dilates in place (255→100 edges, 100→99 dilated); EDGE pixels remain EDGE. So after the production eval, the rendered image is edge+dilated — the chamfer value and the gradient both read the same EDGE pixel set. Consistent. BUT the production eval's chamfer call and the gradient kernel would read the same image state — good. So the analytic arm: 1 render per step (the verification render), then FastImplant (edge+dilate+difference) + chamfer (value) + gradient kernel (needs EDGE pixels + attrs) — all on the same render. 1 render/step total. 

Now the gradient kernel also needs the attribute buffer populated by the MODIFIED FillTriangleKernel — that's the kernel refactor (point 3). The refactor applies to the shared RenderEngine — but WAIT: changing FillTriangleKernel affects the PRODUCTION path (every render writes the attribute buffer now). Is that behavior-neutral? The extra write is to a NEW buffer; the image write is unchanged. It adds ~10 lines and one memory write per filled fragment — a perf cost on the production path! That violates "behavior-neutral" (perf is behavior for a perf-sensitive path — actually it's a measured perf cost, not a semantic change; the render output is bit-identical). The honest design: make the attribute staging CONDITIONAL (a RenderEngine flag enable_fill_attributes_, default false; the polish stage's GPUModel sets it true). Or: a separate kernel variant. Simplest: a bool member + a template/if — but kernels with host-side branching: launch either FillTriangleKernel or FillTriangleKernelWithAttributes (two kernel copies, ~30 lines duplicated) — clean, zero production-path cost. That's the concrete spec: FillTriangleKernelWithAttributes = FillTriangleKernel + 4-line attribute write + one float4 buffer alloc'd in InitializeCUDA only when the flag is set... or always alloc'd (16 MB, one-time) but only WRITTEN when the with-attributes variant is launched. Always-alloc + conditional-launch is simplest and keeps the eval path allocation-free.

Hmm, wait: there's another subtlety — the attribute (u, v, triangleIndex) refers to the fragment's triangle — but the gradient kernel re-resolves (triangleIndex, px, py) from the fragment stream and reads attrs per PIXEL. If two fragments map to the same pixel (overlapping triangles), the LAST writer wins for both image and attrs (same thread) — consistent as argued. But the gradient kernel iterating the fragment stream would process the pixel TWICE (once per fragment covering it) — reading the same attr (the last writer's) twice → double-counting! Fix: the gradient kernel must process each PIXEL once. Options: (a) iterate the fragment stream and skip if the attr's (u,v) doesn't match THIS fragment's (u,v)... fragile; (b) iterate the fragment stream and skip pixels already processed — needs a visited flag (extra buffer + race); (c) iterate the IMAGE grid (width×height threads — but the crop is what matters; the image is 1024² = 1M threads, fine) and check dev_image[p] == EDGE_PIXEL → read attr → accumulate. Image-grid iteration is 1M threads vs fragment stream ~100k-1M — comparable; and it inherently dedupes pixels. The attr read gives (triangleIndex, u, v) of the last writer — exactly matching the silhouette. Option (c) is the clean spec: ChamferGradientKernel iterates the crop region (the same diff-kernel crop the chamfer value uses, so value/gradient pixel sets match) with one thread per pixel, reads EDGE, reads attr, computes ∇D and dp/dθ, accumulates. The crop is ~(bbox ± dilation) ≈ maybe 500×500 = 250k threads. Good.

But hold on — is (c) consistent with the last-writer attr? The silhouette image shows 255 (white) for the pixel if ANY triangle covered it. The attr buffer holds the last writer's (triangle, u, v). The edge pass marks the pixel EDGE if it's white with a black neighbor. The gradient uses the last-writer triangle's dp/dθ. If the last writer's triangle is a backface or interior... no, the last writer IS the triangle that (in stream order) covered the pixel — with backface OFF, both front and back faces write (backfaces get size 1 and fail the inside test, so they never write — only front faces write). With backface ON... production uses ON but the size-1 backface slots never fill. So attrs always come from a front-facing triangle covering the pixel. But the last writer might not be the VISIBLE surface — there's no z-test, so the silhouette is the union of ALL front-facing triangle projections (last-writer is arbitrary among covering triangles). For the chamfer gradient, the standard treatment (Modular Primitives occlusion premise) says the gradient should go to the VISIBLE triangle; without a z-test the MVP's gradient goes to the last-writer triangle — an approximation whose error is bounded by the overlapping-area fraction. This is a known, honest limitation: "the silhouette has no visibility, so the gradient attributes are last-writer; the error is confined to overlap regions (bounded by the leaf-range overlap area); the forward-difference twin check quantifies it." For an implant (mostly convex, small overlap), it's small. If it proves large → the depth-buffer enabler (round-1) becomes necessary (that's the occlusion-aware increment). Good — this ties the depth machinery to a concrete trigger.

Now dD/dx from the distance map: ∇D(p) = ((D[p+ex] − D[p−ex])/2, (D[p+ey] − D[p−ey])/2) with D the uint8 L1 distance map (border-clamped reads; at the image border use one-sided differences). The distance map is in the SAME coordinate orientation as the rendered image (both from the same frame pipeline; the rendered image y-axis: note the render writes dev_image[(py)*width + px] with py from the bottom-left convention... the Frame's distance map comes from OpenCV with origin top-left; the GPUFrame upload presumably handles the flip — the production DistanceMapMetric already reads distance_map[orig_loc] with the rendered image's loc, so whatever convention the production cost uses, the gradient kernel uses the SAME — consistency with the production value is what matters, not the world convention).

The gradient-of-distance-map kernel structure:
```
__global__ void ChamferGradientKernel(
    unsigned char* dev_image,        // EDGE-marked rendered silhouette
    unsigned char* dev_distance_map, // uint8 L1 distance map
    float4* dev_fill_attrs,          // (triangleIndex, u, v, unused) per pixel
    float* dev_triangles,            // model-space vertices (9 per triangle)
    float* dev_gradient,             // 6 floats out (per-block partials or atomic)
    Pose pose, RotationMatrix R,     // current pose for dR/dθ
    float fx, fy, cx, cy,
    int width, int height,
    int crop_lx, int crop_by, int crop_w, int crop_h)
```
Each thread: pixel p in crop; if dev_image[p] != EDGE_PIXEL → return; attr = dev_fill_attrs[p]; triangleIndex = (int)attr.x; u = attr.y; v = attr.z; read 3 vertices from dev_triangles (9 floats); X = R·(u·V1 + v·V2 + (1−u−v)·V3) + t; compute dp/dθ 2×6 via the analytic Jacobian; ∇D via central differences on the distance map; accumulate g += ∇D·(dp/dθ) per DoF. Block-level: shared-memory reduction of 6 floats → one deterministic per-block partial → global ordered reduction kernel (deterministic final gradient), OR the MVP accepts float atomicAdd + a recorded informational hash. Spec: deterministic two-pass (block partials array of 6·numBlocks floats + a 1-block final reduce). float accumulation throughout (explicitly NOT the int truncation of the production path).

Also: the gradient kernel's dR/dθ. The pose convention: R = Rz(θz)·Rx(θx)·Ry(θy) (SetPose). dR/dθx = Rz·dRx/dθx·Ry, etc. — three 3×3 derivatives, 6-12 lines each. The translation Jacobian is identity columns. The projection Jacobian: ∂p_x/∂θ_j = fx·(dX_j·Z − X·dZ_j)/Z²; ∂p_y/∂θ_j = fy·(dY_j·Z − Y·dZ_j)/Z², with the code's signed fx/fy (negative for UF — the sign is already in fx/fy, so the formula is sign-correct as written). Note the code clamps tZ==0 → −1e-6 (a behind-camera degenerate case; the gradient kernel must guard Z < ε → skip the pixel (matches the render's behavior — such a triangle projects wildly; the production render would still draw it... actually with tZ negative the projection flips; the render draws it anyway; the gradient should mirror the render: only skip when Z == 0 exactly; use the same −1e-6 clamp semantics).

Now let me also nail down "which z_trans range" for the gate — the probe sweep. And how it gates GO: gating the z-claim.

arguments.prompt: What exactly does the Modular Primitives rasterizer output per pixel (the primitive/triangle ID and barycentric coordinates u,v — and the zc/wc term)? How does the backward pass compute the gradient with respect to vertex positions — specifically the 2x2 barycentric Jacobian (du/dx, du/dy, dv/dx, dv/dy) and the scatter-add of per-pixel gradients to vertices? text:
The rasterizer outputs per pixel a tuple **(ID, u, v, z_c/w_c)**, where ID identifies the triangle covering the sample, (u,v) are barycentric coordinates, and z_c/w_c is depth in NDC (used only by antialiasing, no gradients). It also outputs a 2×2 Jacobian **J_uv = ∂{u,v}/∂{x,y}** for each pixel.

The backward pass computes gradient **∂L/∂{x_c,y_c,z_c,w_c}** using:
\[∂L/∂{x_c,y_c,z_c,w_c}\] = \[∂L/∂{u,v}\] \[∂{u,v}/∂{x_c,y_c,z_c,w_c}\]  (Equation 2)

It also accounts for ∂L/∂J_uv, and is implemented as a dense operation over pixels using **scatter-add** to accumulate per-pixel gradients to vertices based on triangle IDs, parallelized via a CUDA kernel. The text states the perspective mapping is "readily differentiated analytically" but does not explicitly list the 2x2 barycentric Jacobian (du/dx, du/dy, dv/dx, dv/dy) as a separate formula—the Jacobian J_uv is that quantity.

Source: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277 (Section 3.3, Rasterization)

Actually the cleanest and most standard for "polish with a fixed budget": gradient descent with backtracking on the SURROGATE but acceptance gated on the PRODUCTION cost. Let me not over-engineer — the deliverable is a spec with the key decision points pinned and pre-registered defaults. I'll spec:

- Update rule (MVP): normalized coordinate descent with sign-step: θ_{k+1,i} = clamp(θ_{k,i} − α_k·h_i·sign(g_i), leaf_box), with α_k ∈ {1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16} tried in order until the production cost at θ_{k+1} ≤ production cost at θ_k (each trial = 1 verification render, budget-accounted); if all 5 fail → STOP (the polish has reached a production-cost-local-optimum plateau). α reset to 1 on improvement.
  Hmm, wait — with the FD gradient this doubles the renders (each trial adds a render). The budget: per successful step = 6 (FD) + 1 (verification at θ_k... no — the verification at θ_k happened at the previous step's acceptance; at step k we already HAVE production cost at θ_k). So per step: 6 perturbed renders + 1 trial verification (α=1) = 7 renders, or more with halvings. ~100-140 steps within B_p = 1000. OK.

Actually — let me reconsider whether to verify on PRODUCTION cost at every step. Production cost per eval ≈ surrogate eval cost (same render; the production eval adds white_sum constant + FastImplant + chamfer — the FastImplant difference kernel is the extra launch; white_sum is a per-frame constant computed once). So a production eval ≈ 1 render + edge + dilate + difference + chamfer ≈ slightly more than a surrogate eval. Verifying every step doubles nothing (the verification render IS the next step's base render — the base render at θ_{k+1} is the verification render at θ_{k+1}!). Wait, no: the verification render at θ_{k+1} happens at the END of step k (acceptance check) — that render IS the base for step k+1's gradient (the analytic arm: the gradient kernel runs on the verification render after the production metrics; the FD arm: the FD needs f(θ_{k+1}) = chamfer value — which the verification eval already computed!). So the FD arm: f(θ_k) comes free from the previous step's verification; 6 perturbed renders for g; trial θ_{k+1}; verification render at θ_{k+1} = the base for the next step. Total 7 renders per accepted step (6 FD + 1 verification), 8 with the first step (initial verification). And with the halving trials, +1 render per rejected trial. B_p = 1000 → ~140 accepted steps. Good — matches round-1's estimate.

The analytic arm: 1 render per step (the verification render at θ_{k+1} serves both acceptance AND the next gradient kernel). Per step: 1 render + production metrics + gradient kernel. B_p = 1000 → ~900 steps (or polish_max_steps = 500 cap). Actually — the analytic gradient kernel runs on the CURRENT base render (θ_k, already verified at the end of the previous step): the gradient kernel needs the EDGE-marked image — the verification at θ_k ran FastImplant (edge-marking) + chamfer — the image is edge+dilated; the gradient kernel reads EDGE pixels + attrs. So the gradient at θ_k is computed on the EXISTING verification render with ZERO new renders. Then θ_{k+1} = θ_k − α·h·sign(g) (clamped); verification render at θ_{k+1}; repeat. 1 render per step. Beautiful — that's the honest "1 render/step" claim.

One catch for the analytic arm: the EDGE pixel set after FastImplantDilationMetric includes the dilation pass — the image is mutated to DILATED(99)/EDGE(100) — the chamfer VALUE reads EDGE only, and the gradient must read the same EDGE set — consistent. But the verification's chamfer call consumed the image first (DistanceMapMetric reads, doesn't mutate). The gradient kernel runs after — same image state. Good. Order within a step: Render(θ_k) → FastImplant (edge+dilate+diff) → chamfer value → gradient kernel → (all on the same render). Then update → Render(θ_{k+1}) → verify production cost (FastImplant+chamfer; white_sum constant) → accept/reject.

Another catch: the gradient kernel needs the attribute buffer from the MODIFIED FillTriangleKernel — the Render() must be the "with-attributes" variant when the polish engine is active. Since the polish GPUModel is the leaf CFM's model, and the leaf CFM also runs DIRECT... the attribute staging must be enabled only for polish renders. Design: RenderEngine gains a bool enable_fill_attributes_ (default false) + the FillTriangleKernelWithAttributes variant launched when true; the polish stage sets it once on the shared engine before its loop (and the production DIRECT path never sets it → zero production impact). Since the polish and DIRECT never interleave within a stage (polish is a separate stage after leaf), a single flag flip at stage start is safe. 

Now the deterministic reduction: block-partials + ordered global reduction (2 kernels) OR atomicAdd with informational hash. I'll spec: MVP uses float atomicAdd into dev_chamfer_gradient_ (6 floats), records the gradient hash as informational (the gradient is a direction input, not a scored value; the scored values — surrogate cost, production cost, IoU — are int-deterministic). The deterministic two-pass reduction is the production rule if R13 requires gradient bit-determinism — flag as a follow-up decision, defaulting to the two-pass (cheap: 6 floats × numBlocks). Hmm — actually, let me think about what's truly needed: the polish run's acceptance decisions depend on the gradient DIRECTION; float-atomic nondeterminism changes the direction only at the last-ulp level (tiny perturbations), which won't flip acceptance in practice, but could flip the run_hash of the polish trace → the determinism twin (rerun_identical) would fail → the ablation runner's rerun_identical check would trip. That's a real harness interaction! The ablation.json has rerun_identical as an assertion. So the polish arm's rerun_identical requires the gradient to be bit-deterministic → the two-pass ordered reduction is REQUIRED, not optional, if the polish arm participates in the determinism twin. Clean argument. Spec: deterministic two-pass (per-block partials → fixed-order global reduce), ~20 lines, matches Contradiction 3's doctrine.

Actually, simpler deterministic option: per-block shared-memory reduction to 6 floats, then a single atomicAdd per block — still nondeterministic across blocks. The ordered global reduce (second kernel with a fixed block order, or a single block reading the partial array in order) is deterministic. But wait — is the fragment/pixel iteration order deterministic across the crop grid? Yes: fixed grid, each thread handles a fixed pixel; block partials are deterministic given the input image (int reads, float ops in fixed per-thread order — float addition is deterministic within a thread). So per-block partials are bit-deterministic; the final reduce in fixed order is bit-deterministic. Good — spec the two-kernel reduction.

Also the reset: dev_chamfer_gradient_ and the partial array must be zeroed before each gradient call (cudaMemset 6·(1+nBlocks)·4 bytes ≈ 100 KB — cheap).

Now, let me also compute the ∇D from the distance map precisely: the distance map is CV_8UC1 uint8, L1, truncated at 255. Central differences: ∇D_x = (D[x+1] − D[x−1])/2 — integer ÷ 2 → 0.5 steps; the gradient magnitude ≤ 1 for L1 distance. At the medial axis (maxima), central difference = 0 — fine (those pixels don't contribute; they're interior to the target edge, and the rendered boundary is near the target edge, so boundary pixels sit on the distance-map slope, not the crest). Edge cases: pixels where D[x+1] is a clamp or outside the crop — use one-sided differences at the crop border, mirroring the value metric's crop (the value reads distance_map[orig_loc] for all crop pixels; the gradient reads D at p±1 — which may lie outside the crop but still inside the image (clamp to image bounds). Fine.

Also the distance map in the GPU: GPUFrame* gpu_distance_maps_ — the GPUFrame presumably wraps the uploaded uint8 distance map. Its GetDeviceImagePointer is used by DistanceMapMetric_Kernel. The gradient kernel reads the same buffer. Confirmed the type.

Now — the precondition gate, concretely wired to angle 03's probe:
- Extension: the z-profile probe gains a "term-decomposition" mode: per sweep point, record (a) full DIRECT_DILATION cost, (b) chamfer-only term (DistanceMapMetric value), (c) dilated-overlap-only term (FastImplantDilationMetric value) — all from the same render + the two metric calls (order: FastImplant then DistanceMap, the production order; FastImplant mutates the image but DistanceMap reads EDGE only, unaffected by the dilation writes). Zero extra renders.
- Gate (pre-registered, evaluated at dilation = 1, frames = the ablation frame set, anchor = fem.jts frame-0 z):
  - G1: valley_depth(chamfer) ≥ 0.10 (2× the z-blind threshold 0.05, margin against the 1-mm sweep discretization);
  - G2: valley_depth(chamfer) − valley_depth(dilated) ≥ 0.05 (the "deeper than the dilated-overlap valley" requirement, above discretization);
  - G3: |argmin_offset(chamfer)| ≤ 2 mm (valley centered on the truth z within the sweep step);
  - G4: p1 holds (cost(0) is the sweep minimum within noise — the chamfer curve is V-shaped, not monotone).
- If G1–G4 hold → the z-claim of the polish arm is pre-registered as testable; the arm's z-gap is expected to shrink vs DIRECT-only@35k. If they fail → the polish arm still runs (measurement-first), but the pre-registered expectation flips: polish wins only in-plane/evals; any z-gap change is recorded as noise; the "polish fixes z" narrative is DEAD (this is the honest GO-gate semantics: the gate gates the CLAIM, not the measurement).
- Threshold numbers are pre-registered; run 1 records, later runs enforce (pin-first per angle 03 p3 protocol).

Which z range: the probe's existing ±15 mm sweep (31 points) — matches the leaf z-range ±15 (baseline.json ranges leaf_z 15) and brackets the 6.31 mm observed gap by 2.4×. Near-field sub-range |Δz| ≤ 6.31 mm is additionally reported (the region the DIRECT leaf actually needs to refine).

Now, the "how it gates GO" — the full GO rule for landing polish in production (round-1): precondition probe G1–G4 AND the ablation arm C-vs-A-vs-B outcome. If G fails: the arm runs once as evidence, then the polish z-claim is closed; in-plane/evals claims still judged by the arm.

Now let me also make sure I handle "which DOF perturbations" precisely for the FD MVP: e_i in Pose field order (x_loc, y_loc, z_loc, x_ang, y_ang, z_ang); h defaults (x,y: 0.5 mm; z: 5.0 mm; angles: 0.5°) with the pre-registered h-calibration; FORWARD differences g_i = (f(θ+h e_i) − f(θ))/h using the cached base f(θ); central differences as the verification twin (12 renders) only for the gradient-twin check (a few times per run, not per step).

Now, everything is in place. Let me also reference the papers PDFs properly:
- Laine 2011 HPG: the four-stage software rasterizer; the existing render engine mirrors it (per round-1). For Round 2, the relevant part: their per-pixel barycentric evaluation + the "no z-buffer in the base pipeline" detail... Actually for the kernel-refactor section, the relevant citation is Modular Primitives (the successor paper). Laine 2011's relevance to the polish: the fragment-stream organization the gradient kernel reuses. I'll cite it as context.
- Modular Primitives TOG 39(6): (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + J_uv + scatter-add backward (verified again just now from ar5iv).

Let me now also decide the exact title and structure of the Round 2 section:

## Round 2 — Executable MVP spec for the polish stage (persona: differentiable-rendering researcher; verdicts → spec)

Sections:
** R2-1 The precondition gate, made measurable (z-profile probe on the chamfer surrogate; thresholds; range; gating semantics)
** R2-2 Forward-difference MVP (6 renders/step): surrogate eval path (chamfer; which metric reads it; edge-pass dependency), DOF perturbations + step sizes + h-calibration, budget arithmetic (7 renders/step incl. verification; B_p=1000 → ~140 steps), the RenderPrimaryCamera seam
** R2-3 What 'staging the barycentrics' means as a concrete kernel refactor (FillTriangleKernelWithAttributes; attribute buffer; last-writer pairing argument; the visibility caveat; zero production-path cost via conditional variant)
** R2-4 Analytic projection Jacobian + gradient-of-distance-map kernel (1 render/step): the math, the kernel structure, the rigid-body simplification vs NVDiffrast (no J_uv term, no vertex scatter-add), float-accumulation + deterministic two-pass reduction (rerun_identical interaction), backface/leaf-dilation matching rules, gradient-twin check (FD vs analytic)
** R2-5 The ablation arm that arbitrates contradiction 6 — three-arm design (A: DIRECT@35k, B: DIRECT@34k, C: DIRECT@34k+polish@1000), equal cumulative budget, IoU ≥ 0.85 gate, per-axis gaps, sample-size/power (N=12 paired units; 3 frames × 4 start poses; what is conclusive at what effect size), pre-registered decision rules
** R2-6 Zotero pull list with per-paper expected value (what each changes about the MVP or NO-GO list)
** What Could Not Be Verified (Round 2)
** Sources (Round 2 additions)
