## Round 2 — Executable Specifications (measurement-apparatus)

### Summary

This round turns Round 1's sketches into executable specs from the test-infrastructure seat: (1) the perturbation suite that calibrates the IoU 0.85 gate's checked coverage — a per-variant IoU-vs-Δ transfer-function grid plus targeted regression injections, whose deliverable is the minimal-detectable-regression table per axis; (2) the z-profile probe as a runnable spec — 31-render Δz sweep on the verified RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (optimizer_manager.cpp:1235-1246), valley-depth metric, and the chamfer-heavy ≥ Mahfouz ≥ pure-overlap ranking mapped onto the verified metric composition of the 7 variants; (3) a Round-1 correction with source proof: the Directive::SymTrap seam addition ALREADY EXISTS in the current tree (optimizer_run_controller_core.h:60-63 → "Sym_Trap" → optimizer_manager.cpp:177-185), so the work is now pins and the tibia-after-femur drive sequence, not a code change; (4) the complete ablation.json field list with the ci/nightly profile split and the additive gpu ctest label design; (5) the cross-GPU noise-floor plan — what the banded L1 gate needs, what an IoU retune looks like, and exactly what the single RTX 3090 can and cannot measure today.

### Key Findings

#### R2-1 — Perturbation suite (oracle-of-the-oracle): two halves, one deliverable — the minimal-detectable-regression table
- What the gate can and cannot see today, from measured numbers: recovered IoU 0.9936 vs gate 0.85 (margin 0.1436, baseline.json measured block); start-pose↔label correspondence pinned empirically at IoU == 1.0 (oracle_test.cpp correspondence procedure, REQUIRE(best_iou > 0.50)); the 6.31 mm z gap passes the gate at 0.9936. So the honest pre-registration expectations, each to be confirmed by the suite: (a) z regressions up to at least the 6.31 mm gap are INVISIBLE to the gate by design (magnification <1% at ~1.1 m SID, inside the dilation-6 absorption radius — Round 1's mechanism, still derived not measured); (b) in-plane/rotation regressions become visible once the silhouette displacement exceeds the dilation-absorption radius (≈6 px at dilation 6 — the rendered image and comparison frame are both dilated by the FastImplantDilationMetric dilation argument, so overlap is preserved for sub-radius shifts); (c) structural regressions (budget/SetCallOffset, dilation-schedule, frame↔label mapping, backface, edge-config) trip the gate hard because they move the recovered pose by stage-range magnitudes (15-35 mm, settings_constants.h TRUNK_RANGE/BRANCH_RANGE/Z_SEARCH_RANGE) — far beyond any absorption radius; (d) cost-VALUE regressions (the live distance-map index bug, distance_map_metric.cu:27) are INVISIBLE to the gate — the gate compares rendered silhouette vs label, never cost values — which is exactly why Tier-0 pins (02) and ablation.json exist. [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json, test/oracle/oracle_test.cpp, include/domain/settings_constants.h:24-37; prior-run angle 02]
- Suite shape, half 1 — per-variant perturbation grid (the transfer function): anchor at the fem.jts golden pose (frame 0), per variant v ∈ the 7 registered (CostFunctionManager.cpp:344-423) and per axis i ∈ {x, y, z, xa, ya, za}, render + IoU at Δ ∈ {±1, ±2, ±5, ±6.31(z), ±10, ±15} mm/deg, one axis perturbed at a time (12-18 renders per (variant, axis)); record IoU(Δ) into ablation.json perturbation_calibration[]. Assertions (per-variant, executable): (m1) IoU is monotone non-increasing in |Δ| beyond the plateau (a non-monotone curve flags a render/convention bug, not a gate issue); (m2) plateau: IoU ≥ 0.99 for |Δ| ≤ dilation-absorption radius (in-plane) — pins the absorption mechanism; (m3) z-characteristic pin: IoU(Δz = 6.31) ≥ 0.99 — the measured z-blindness becomes a pinned characteristic, and if a future z remedy (SAME_Z weight, chamfer reweight) makes this assertion fail, that is the z-axis becoming visible, which the suite must report as an event, not a failure. Deliverable: per-axis minimal-detectable-regression (smallest |Δ| with IoU < 0.85) — the direct answer to "what size of regression trips the gate".
- Suite shape, half 2 — targeted injections (checked-coverage): each injection is a poisoned oracle run at the flat-3000 shape, asserting the gate's behavior: NEG (negative control, unpoisoned — MUST pass, guards against false positives); INJ-BUDGET (cost lambda capped at 100 calls — SetCallOffset/stage-loop regression proxy — MUST fail); INJ-DILATION (comparison dilated at 0 and 12 instead of 6 — MUST fail, and if 12 does not fail that itself is a finding: the gate's dilation sensitivity is asymmetric); INJ-LABEL (wrong frame's label — MUST fail, proves the empirical correspondence is load-bearing); INJ-BACKFACE (backface ON vs the oracle's OFF — expected fail or near-fail on an open/concave STL; doubles as contradiction-4's evidence check (b), recommended by angle 02); INJ-EDGE (Canny aperture/threshold altered — expected fail); INJ-VARIANT (swap to a z-blind variant — may NOT fail: a variant regression invisible to the gate is the informative case, and it is exactly what the ablation z-gap column exists to catch). Assertion philosophy per Schuler & Dallmeier checked-coverage: a gate that never fails is untested; the suite must contain at least one injection that fails, one that passes, and one whose outcome is a measurement. [Source: repo — test/oracle/oracle_test.cpp (kBudget/kIouGate/build pipeline), src/compute/CostFunctionManager.cpp:344-423, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:73-104; https://www.st.cs.uni-saarland.de/publications/files/schuler-stvr-2013.pdf]
- Cost and schedule: half 1 ≈ 7 variants × 6 axes × ~15 Δ ≈ 630 renders ≈ well under 10 min at the verified ~20-60 evals/s budget-3000 rate (qml_parity_check.cpp:126 "a few minutes on the RTX 3090"); half 2 ≈ 7 injected 3000-budget runs ≈ tens of minutes. Per-PR reduced shape: half 1 on DIRECT_DILATION frame 0 only; full suite nightly. Headless Tier-0 twin: the IoU-vs-shift math (dilated-overlap IoU on synthetic strips) runs in the CPU metric reference, so the transfer-function fitter is testable without the GPU; the render+metric path stays GPU-authoritative. [Source: repo — test/oracle/qml_parity_check.cpp:124-126, test/CMakeLists.txt:1253-1254; verified evals/s derivation in Round 1]
- Confidence: high on the mechanics (all seams source-verified); medium on the pre-registration expectations (they are the suite's hypotheses; the minimal-detectable-regression numbers are unmeasured until the suite runs).
- Relevance to this project: this closes the synthesis open question "What size of regression trips the IoU 0.85 gate?" — the suite is the instrument, and it simultaneously hardens the gate doctrine (appearance arbiter) by proving which regression classes the oracle can and cannot see, so the other five angles' gates are understood, not assumed.

#### R2-2 — z-profile probe as an executable spec: 31-render sweep, valley-depth metric, and the ranking hypothesis mapped to verified metric composition
- Entry point (source-verified): the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda at optimizer_manager.cpp:1235-1246 — pose set (physical Point6D → SetCurrentPrimaryCameraPose), biplane secondary via calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B, then stage_manager.callActiveCostFunction(). The public twin EvaluateCostFunctionAtPoint(point, stage) at optimizer_manager.cpp:1372-1387 (pose set + stage dispatch) is the simpler seam for the driver-seam probe variant; the compute-only template is oracle_test.cpp's hand-rolled lambda at oracle_test.cpp:286-291. So defaults: h = (0.5, 0.5, 8.0, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5). With h-calibration ranges: translations {0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0} mm; z {2, 4, 8, 12} mm; angles {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}°.

Quantization floor: f = ΣD/(N+0.1), N ≈ boundary pixels ≈ perimeter ≈ 2π·r ≈ 1200 (r ≈ 200 px); per-pixel D changes ±1 per px of boundary motion; the per-eval floor ≈ 1/1200 ≈ 8e-4; h-calibration requires |Δf| ≥ 10·floor ≈ 8e-3 (at h_z=8, boundary motion 1.3 px × N pixels × ~0.5 mean distance change → |Δf| ≈ 1.3·0.5 ≈ 0.65 — wait that's the cost change per pixel summed over N pixels divided by N: the MEAN chamfer change = mean over boundary pixels of ΔD ≈ 0.5-1.3 per pixel → Δf ≈ 0.5-1.3, way above the floor. Good — the chamfer is genuinely smooth-ish in z at these steps.)

Hmm wait, careful: for a pure scale change (z motion), the boundary moves OUTWARD (or inward) by δ px; each boundary pixel's L1 distance to the target edge changes by ≈ ±δ (some pixels move closer, others farther, depending on local curvature + edge position); the mean |ΔD| ≈ δ/2-ish; the SIGNED sum ≈ small (scale change is symmetric-ish)... Actually the chamfer cost = mean distance of rendered boundary to the target edge. For a z shift, the rendered boundary scales about the image center; the mean signed distance change is ≈ 0 to first order?? No — if the target edge is the TRUE boundary at the truth pose, then at the truth pose the rendered boundary coincides with the target edge → mean distance ≈ 0 (the chamfer minimum). Moving z scales the boundary → mean absolute distance grows ≈ δ·(fraction of boundary where the edge is locally ~parallel... ). The chamfer is NOT symmetric in the sign of z... it grows approximately linearly with |δ| (mean distance of a circle of radius r±δ to a circle of radius r ≈ |δ|). So valley: cost(Δz) ≈ c·|Δz|·0.167 px/mm... c·Δz·(2.68/16)... I'll state: at the truth pose the chamfer is ~0 (boundary on target), and it grows roughly linearly with boundary displacement — so valley_depth ≈ 1 if the extremes dominate, and the G1 ≥ 0.10 threshold is a weak bar; the real question (G2) is whether the dilated-overlap valley at dilation 1 is comparably deep. Honest statement: the GATE NUMBERS ARE UNKNOWN; the thresholds are pre-registered hypotheses; run 1 records. That's the point.

Also I should note the uint8 truncation: distanceTransform CV_8UC1 caps at 255 → the chamfer dynamic range is capped; for valley_depth the (max−min) normalization absorbs it. One line.

## Round 2 — Executable MVP Spec for the Polish Stage (differentiable-polish)

### Summary

This round converts Round 1's verdicts into an executable MVP spec, from the differentiable-rendering/CUDA seat, with every number grounded in the verified repo: (1) the precondition gate is now measurable — a term-decomposed z-profile probe (chamfer-only vs dilated-overlap-only valley depths from the *same* 31-render sweep) with pre-registered thresholds (valley_depth ≥ 0.10, chamfer − dilated ≥ 0.05, |argmin_offset| ≤ 2 mm, evaluated at the leaf dilation 1 over the ±15 mm sweep) that gates the arm's **z-claim**, never the arm itself; (2) the forward-difference MVP is pinned down — the surrogate is the existing chamfer term (GPUMetrics::DistanceMapMetric, whose kernel reads only EDGE_PIXEL-marked renders and therefore requires the existing EdgeKernel first; live call at DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80, dead duplicate :101-104), the 6-renders-per-step arithmetic is exact (6 perturbed RenderPrimaryCamera calls + the cached base from the previous step's verification = 7 renders per accepted step → ~140 steps within B_p = 1000), and the step sizes come from the actual calibration (1198 mm SID, 0.373 mm pitch: 1 px = 0.373 mm, ~6 mm of z per px of boundary motion at r ≈ 200 px); (3) "staging the barycentrics" is a concrete refactor — a sibling kernel FillTriangleKernelWithAttributes that writes float4(triangleIndex, a/denominator, b/denominator, 0) per filled pixel into a 16 MB buffer, launched only when a polish flag is set (zero production-path cost), with a last-writer pairing argument that keeps image and attributes consistent; (4) the analytic kernel (1 render/step) is specified end-to-end — the 2×6 projection Jacobian for the Rz·Rx·Ry pose composition, ∇D from the uint8 L1 distance map, a crop-matched pixel-grid kernel, and a bit-deterministic two-pass float reduction (mandatory because the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin would trip on float-atomic accumulation — Contradiction 3 bites the gradient too); (5) the contradiction-6 arbitration is redesigned as a THREE-arm paired study (A: DIRECT@35k, B: DIRECT@34k, C: DIRECT@34k+polish@1000) — the B arm controls for the budget-gift confound the round-1 two-arm design could not see; N = 12 paired units (3 Kneel_1 frames × 4 start seeds) gives 0.8 power at a 1σ effect, and anything smaller is honestly reported as underpowered; (6) the Zotero pulls get per-paper expected value — NVDiffrast validates the scatter-add design and supplies the AA fallback spec, arXiv:1906.07870 decides whether the boundary term is needed, Gablonsky sets the STOP/re-seed rules, Veriserum sets the achievable-precision prior and confirms z stays the weak axis, SoftRas/DIB-R stay fallback-only, DiffDRR/DiffPose harden the photometric NO-GO.

### Key Findings

#### R2-1 — The precondition gate, made measurable: a term-decomposed z-profile probe, pre-registered thresholds, and an honest gating semantics (it gates the z-claim, not the measurement)
- Instrument: angle 03's z-profile probe (31-render Δz sweep, entry points verified at optimizer_manager.cpp:1235-1246 / :1372-1387 / oracle_test.cpp:286-291), extended with a **term-decomposition mode**: at each of the 31 sweep points, record three costs from the SAME render — the full DIRECT_DILATION cost, the chamfer-only term (DistanceMapMetric return), and the dilated-overlap-only term (FastImplantDilationMetric return). Zero extra renders: both metrics already run per eval in the production order (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:73-83), and FastImplantDilationMetric's in-place edge/dilation pass leaves the EDGE_PIXEL set the chamfer reads untouched (EdgeKernel writes WHITE→EDGE, DilateKernel writes WHITE/BLACK→DILATED, EDGE=100 is never rewritten; pixel_grayscale_colors.h). The probe lambda that records per-term values is a new ~15-line probe-only body (in the probe's TU, not production), replicating the verified lambda shape. [Source: repo — src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:73-83, src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, include/compute/pixel_grayscale_colors.h:9-12; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-2]
- Sweep range: the EXISTING ±15 mm step-1 sweep (31 renders, anchor = fem.jts frame-0 z = −1027.713, other axes at truth — baseline.json expected_pose_per_frame frame 0). This is not an arbitrary range: it is exactly the leaf z-range (baseline.json settings.ranges.leaf_z = 15) and brackets the observed 6.31 mm gap 2.4× — the polish operates post-leaf inside this box, so the gate measures the signal in the region the polish will actually search. [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json settings.ranges + expected_pose_per_frame + tolerances.observed_max_gap_vs_golden; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-2]
- Dilation: the gate is evaluated at **leaf dilation 1** (the polish runs post-leaf; leaf dilation = 1 per baseline.json dilation_px). The {6,3,1,4} dilations from angle 03's probe are recorded as context: a valley that exists only at dilation 6/4 but not 1 means the z-signal lives in the trunk/branch regime where polish does not run — that reversal is a measured non-win for the polish z-claim, not a pass. Honest complication surfaced this round: at dilation 1 the dilated-overlap is NOT maximally flat (its pixels flip at ~1 px of boundary motion ≈ 6 mm of z, per the calibration arithmetic in R2-2), so "the chamfer valley is deeper than the dilated-overlap valley" is a real empirical question at the polish's own dilation — which is exactly why the gate is pre-registered, not assumed. [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json dilation_px + ranges; calibration.txt]
- Gate metrics (pre-registered, on the chamfer-only term; valley_depth = (max − cost(0))/(max − min) over the 31 points, the angle-03 formula): **G1** valley_depth ≥ 0.10 (2× the angle-03 z-blind classification threshold 0.05, margin against the 1-mm sweep discretization); **G2** valley_depth(chamfer) − valley_depth(dilated) ≥ 0.05 (the "deeper than" requirement, above discretization — ratio also recorded for reference); **G3** |argmin_offset(chamfer)| ≤ 2 mm (valley centered on the truth z within 2 sweep steps); **G4** (angle-03 p1) cost(0) is the sweep minimum within the noise floor (5 repeats, expect 0 spread — int-atomic path). Run 1 records, later runs enforce (angle-03 pin-first doctrine). [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-2 p1/p2]
- Gating semantics — the honest version: G1–G4 gate the arm's **z-claim**, not the arm. If all hold, the pre-registered expectation for arm C is a z-gap shrink vs arm A. If any fails, the arm still runs (measurement-first — the in-plane and evals-to-gate claims are independent of z observability), but the z-gap column is pre-registered as "expected unchanged within the noise floor", and a polish that moves z despite a failed gate is a contradiction to investigate, not a win. This prevents the polish z-narrative from being smuggled past observability while keeping the measurement. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-2 (the probe is "the gate on every z remedy"); synthesis Contradiction 2 (report evals and z-error separately)]
- Threshold sanity-check (why 0.10 is a weak bar, and that is fine): at the truth pose the rendered boundary sits ON the target edge, so the chamfer ≈ 0 and grows roughly linearly with boundary displacement (~0.167 px boundary motion per mm of z at r ≈ 200 px, SID 1198 — R2-2 arithmetic), so a healthy chamfer z-curve is V-shaped and valley_depth → ~1; G1 only filters out curves that are flat-with-noise. G2 is the discriminating gate. One caveat recorded: the distance map is CV_8UC1 (distanceTransform DIST_L1, mask 5 — Frame::SetDistanceMap, frame_headless.cpp:129-137), so distances truncate at 255; the (max−min) normalization in valley_depth absorbs the capped dynamic range, and the plateau contributes zero gradient (constant region) — both are benign for a local-refinement gate. [Source: repo — test/unit/frame_headless.cpp:129-137; calibration.txt]
- Confidence: high on the mechanics (every entry point, metric composition, and the EDGE-set non-interference verified by direct read this round); medium on the threshold VALUES (pre-registered hypotheses; run 1 records).
- Relevance to this project: this is synthesis recommendation 8's precondition ("the z-profile probe shows the chamfer surrogate's valley deeper than the dilated-overlap valley") turned into a runnable gate with numbers, range, and honest gating semantics — and it rides on angle 03's instrument with a ~15-line probe-only addition, no production change.

#### R2-2 — The forward-difference MVP, concretely: the surrogate eval path, which DOF perturbations, step sizes from the real calibration, and the exact 6-renders-per-step budget arithmetic
- The surrogate, confirmed: f(θ) = GPUMetrics::DistanceMapMetric(rendered(θ), gpu_distance_maps_->at(frame), 1) — the chamfer term ALONE (not the production sum). The reader is DistanceMapMetric_Kernel (src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu): it counts only pixels where the rendered image == EDGE_PIXEL(100) and int-atomicAdds the uint8 L1 distance-map value, returning distance_map_score/(edge_pixel_count+0.1); the live call is DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80 (the :101-104 duplicate is dead-commented). The distance map is built once per frame by Frame::SetDistanceMap (OpenCV distanceTransform on the inverted edge image, CV_8UC1) and uploaded as a GPUFrame (CostFunctionManager.h:163 gpu_distance_maps_ = vector<GPUFrame*>) — the polish NEVER recomputes it. [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:73-104, include/compute/CostFunctionManager.h:163, test/unit/frame_headless.cpp:129-137]
- The dependency the polish must not forget: DistanceMapMetric_Kernel reads EDGE_PIXEL, and the rendered binary silhouette becomes EDGE-marked only by FastImplantDilationMetric_EdgeKernel (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu), which the production path runs first. In the production order this comes for free; a polish surrogate wrapper must launch it explicitly. The wrapper is ~35 lines, ZERO new kernels: GPUMetrics::ChamferSurrogate(rendered, distance_map, dilation) = ResetPixelScoreKernel + FastImplantDilationMetric_EdgeKernel + DistanceMapMetric_Reset + DistanceMapMetric_Kernel + 2 D2H — all kernels already exist and EdgeKernel is declared in fast_implant_dilation_metric.cuh, so the wrapper can live in distance_map_metric.cu or the polish TU. The dilation argument is only used for the crop clamps (the value is unaffected by the dilation pass; DILATED=99 pixels are excluded from the chamfer by construction). [Source: repo — src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu (EdgeKernel + DilateKernel semantics), include/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cuh (EdgeKernel declared), src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu]
- How the 6 renders happen: the polish loop calls GPUModel::RenderPrimaryCamera(θ + h_i·e_i) — the SAME seam costFunctionDIRECT_DILATION uses (gpu_model.cu:115-123: SetPose + Render) — 6 sequential calls on the leaf CostFunctionManager's GPUModel, reusing the leaf CFM's GPU objects (the round-1 seam: no OptimizerRunLaunch signature change). Sequential only: 6-pose streamed/parallel rendering is angle 05's batching territory and is explicitly out of MVP scope. [Source: repo — src/compute/gpu_model.cu:115-123; angle 06 Round 1 "hybrid loop"]
- DOF perturbations and step sizes (pre-registered defaults + a one-time h-calibration): e_i in Pose field order (x_location, y_location, z_location, x_angle, y_angle, z_angle — Pose struct in render_engine.cuh; the golden's JT_EULER_312 field LISTING order z,x,y is a known confusion trap: never perturb "golden-order" fields, always the struct order, with R = Rz·Rx·Ry per SetPose). Defaults from the verified calibration (JT_INTCALIB 1198 mm principal distance, 0.373 mm pitch → fx = fy ≈ −3212 px, 1 px = 0.373 mm at the detector, boundary motion per mm of z ≈ r_px/Z ≈ 200/1198 ≈ 0.167 px): h = (0.5, 0.5, 8.0, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5) — mm, mm, mm, deg, deg, deg — moving the boundary ~1.3, 1.3, ~1.3, and ~0.8-1.2 px respectively (0.5° = 8.7 mrad × 35 mm radius ≈ 0.3 mm ≈ 0.8 px). Rationale: forward differences are meaningful only when the boundary moves ≥ 1 px, because the L1 distance-map values change by ±1 per pixel of boundary motion and the chamfer's per-eval quantization floor is ~1/(N_edge+0.1) ≈ 8e-4 (N_edge ≈ 1200 boundary pixels at r ≈ 200 px). h-calibration (pre-registered, one-time per frame, recorded in ablation.json): at the golden pose, sweep h per axis over {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2} mm / {2, 4, 8, 12} mm (z) / {0.25, 0.5, 1}°, pick the largest h with |Δf| ≥ 10× the floor AND central-difference agreement between h and h/2 within 20% (linear-regime check). [Source: repo — example_studies/Kneel_1/calibration.txt, include/compute/render_engine.cuh (Pose + SetPose math), test/golden/baseline.json golden_units]
- The 6-renders-per-step arithmetic (exact): step k starts with f(θ_k) already cached — it was computed by step k−1's acceptance verification (the verification eval is a full production eval, whose chamfer term IS the surrogate value at θ_k; identical to the minimal wrapper's value because the dilation pass never rewrites EDGE pixels). Per step: 6 perturbed surrogate renders (forward differences g_i = (f(θ_k + h_i e_i) − f(θ_k))/h_i) + 1 trial verification render at θ_{k+1} = clamp(θ_k − α·h·sign(g), leaf_box) with α ∈ {1, ½, ¼, ⅛, 1/16} tried in order until the production cost is non-increasing (acceptance arbiter = production cost, round-1 rule) = **7 renders per accepted step** (8 for the first step, which needs the initial verification), +1 render per rejected α-trial. At B_p = polish_budget_ = 1000 eval-calls (every surrogate AND verification eval increments cost_function_calls_, round-1 rule), the FD arm sustains ~140 accepted steps. The leaf-box clamp (leaf ranges x,y ±3, z ±15, rotations ±3 — baseline.json ranges) keeps the polish inside the region DIRECT already explored. Central differences (12 renders/step) are used ONLY for the gradient-twin check (R2-4), a few times per run, never per step. [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json settings.ranges + budget_per_stage; angle 06 Round 1 "hybrid loop" + "budget semantics"]
- The sign-step update rule is a deliberate MVP choice (brutally honest): the gradient's mixed units (chamfer-mm per mm vs per degree) make unscaled steepest descent fragile; a normalized coordinate sign-step −α·h_i·sign(g_i) with production-cost-monotone acceptance is robust, needs no line-search machinery, and degrades gracefully to a pattern search near the plateau (where it stops via the α-exhaustion rule). The ADAM upgrade (per-axis normalization, Veriserum-informed) is spec'd in R2-6 as the follow-on if the sign-step plateaus. [Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.05483 (Veriserum optimizer discussion); angle 06 Round 1 verdicts]
- Confidence: high on every mechanical fact (surrogate reader, EdgeKernel dependency, render seam, calibration arithmetic all verified by direct read); medium on the step-size DEFAULTS until the h-calibration runs (they are parameterized by the verified calibration but the linear-regime check is a measurement).
- Relevance to this project: this is the executable ~1-week MVP (round-1 verdict) — it reuses Render(), both existing metric kernels, the leaf CFM, and the injected-cost accounting, and its only new code is the ~35-line ChamferSurrogate wrapper + the polish loop; it establishes the gradient-twin baseline that the analytic arm (R2-4) must beat on cost.

#### R2-3 — What "staging the barycentrics FillTriangleKernel already computes" means as a concrete kernel refactor: a sibling kernel, a 16 MB buffer, and the last-writer pairing argument
- Current state (verified by direct read): FillTriangleKernel (render_engine.cu) computes the unnormalized barycentrics a, b, c and denominator for the inside test — a = (y2−y3)(px−x3) + (x3−x2)(py−y3), b = (y3−y1)(px−x3) + (x1−x3)(py−y3), c = denominator − a − b, with the two-branch inside test (denominator > 0 and < 0) — and writes only 255 to dev_image[(py)*width + px]. The per-pixel (triangleIndex, u = a/denominator, v = b/denominator) it needs for a gradient pass is computed and thrown away. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel]
- The refactor, concretely (this is the whole "staging" story): (a) one new buffer dev_fill_attrib_ of width_×height_×float4 (16 MB at 1024² — same allocation pattern as the existing dev_z_line_values_ width×height float buffer; ~4 lines in InitializeCUDA, one cudaFree in FreeCuda; the eval path stays allocation-free); (b) a SIBLING kernel FillTriangleKernelWithAttributes — a copy of FillTriangleKernel with ~8 added lines: inside the accepted branch (both denominator signs), after the 255 write, write float4(triangleIndex, a/denominator, b/denominator, 0.f) to dev_fill_attrib_[py*width + px]; (c) RenderEngine gains bool enable_fill_attributes_ (default false), and Render() launches the WithAttributes variant when set, the stock kernel otherwise. The stride/prefix/bounding-box launch scheme is untouched. Zero production-path cost: the stock kernel and the stock launch are bit-identical to today, and the flag is flipped once by the polish stage on the shared engine (the polish and DIRECT stages never interleave, so a single flag set at stage start is safe). [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu (InitializeCUDA/FreeCuda/Render), include/compute/render_engine.cuh (dev_z_line_values_ precedent)]
- The consistency argument that makes this correct WITHOUT atomics: the current fill is last-writer-wins in the deterministic fragment-stream order (no atomics in FillTriangleKernel; thread i of the fill grid owns fragment i, and the stream order is fixed by the prefix sums). Writing the image byte and the attribute float4 from the SAME thread preserves the pairing: at any pixel, the attribute (triangle, u, v) belongs to the same triangle that produced the silhouette value there. The render stays bit-deterministic, and the attribute buffer is bit-deterministic with it (the ablation runner's run_hash/re_reruns_identical discipline carries over). [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel + StridePrefixKernel; angles/05-compute-perf.org determinism finding]
- The honest caveat — visibility: without a z-test, the "last writer" among all front-face triangles covering a pixel is arbitrary; the gradient flows to that triangle's 3D points. For a near-convex implant the overlap area is small and the error is bounded by the overlap fraction of the silhouette; the FD-twin check (R2-4) quantifies it. If it proves large, the fix is the round-1 depth-buffer enabler (a min-z test in the fill + ownership via z — the documented occlusion-upgrade path, explicitly NOT part of the MVP). [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "depth channel" finding (occlusion-aware visibility gradients)]
- What the MVP deliberately does NOT take from Modular Primitives (the honest cost saving): the reference rasterizer outputs (ID, u, v, zc/wc) PLUS a 2×2 barycentric Jacobian J_uv = ∂{u,v}/∂{x,y} per pixel, and its backward chain (Eq. 2) flows ∂L/∂{x_c,y_c,z_c,w_c} = ∂L/∂{u,v}·∂{u,v}/∂{x_c,y_c,z_c,w_c} plus a ∂L/∂J_uv term, scatter-added to vertices by triangle ID. That chain exists because their triangles are DEFORMABLE (vertex positions are the optimization variables). The MVP optimizes a RIGID 6-DoF pose: the 3D point on the triangle is X = R·(u·V1 + v·V2 + (1−u−v)·V3) + t with FIXED model-space vertices (dev_triangles_ is static), so the gradient flows through the pose transform only — no J_uv term, no per-vertex scatter-add, just a 6-DoF accumulation. The staged tuple is (triangleIndex, u, v) — exactly the Modular-Primitives per-pixel output minus zc/wc and J_uv. [Source: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277 (rasterizer output tuple, Eq. 2, scatter-add backward — re-verified this round); repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu (dev_triangles_ static)]
- Confidence: high (all kernel facts source-verified this round; the pairing argument is a direct consequence of the deterministic fragment stream).
- Relevance to this project: this is the ~10-line kernel change + ~30-line plumbing that makes the analytic arm's 1-render/step gradient possible, at zero cost to the production render path — and it is the one change in the whole polish MVP that touches the shared rasterizer, so it carries the strictest review bar (bit-identical production renders + oracle green + the Tier-0 barycentric pin from angle 02's test inventory).

#### R2-4 — The analytic projection Jacobian + gradient-of-distance-map kernel (1 render/step): the math, the kernel structure, float-accumulation rules, production-parity matching, and the FD-twin gate
- The math (all conventions from the verified code): pose θ = (tx, ty, tz, rx, ry, rz) in Pose field order; R = Rz(rz)·Rx(rx)·Ry(ry) exactly as SetPose builds it; X = R·v + t for model-space v; projection p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy) with the code's SIGNED fx/fy (negative for the UF calibration — the sign is already inside the constant, so the formulas are sign-correct as written; WorldToPixelKernel). The 2×6 projection Jacobian: ∂p_x/∂θ_j = fx·(X'_j·Z − X·Z'_j)/Z², ∂p_y/∂θ_j = fy·(Y'_j·Z − Y·Z'_j)/Z², where (X'_j, Y'_j, Z'_j) = dX/dθ_j; the three translation columns are unit vectors; the three rotation columns are dR/dr·v with dR/drx = Rz·(dRx/drx)·Ry, dR/dry = Rz·Rx·(dRy/dry), dR/drz = (dRz/drz)·Rx·Ry — three 3×3 derivative matrices, ~20 lines of trig, computed host-side once per step and passed as kernel params (or as a 2×6 float array). Mirror the render's degenerate-guard: Z == 0 → −1e-6 clamp (WorldToPixelKernel), so the gradient never divides by zero where the render drew something. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu WorldToPixelKernel + SetPose; include/compute/render_engine.cuh Pose/RotationMatrix]
